title: Sega 315-5124 VDP register file
covers: The eleven VDP registers R0 to R10 of the Mark III and Master System video chip, their bits and power-on values, and what MAME does for them

rows.text: R0 and R1 set the VDP display and interrupt mode.
R0 bit 7, VSI, set to 1 keeps the right 8 character columns fixed; 0 scrolls them along with the background.
R0 bit 6, HSI, set to 1 keeps the top 2 character rows fixed; 0 scrolls them along with the background.
R0 bit 5, LCB, set to 1 blanks the left character column in the border color; 0 gives normal display.
R0 bit 4, IE1, is the interrupt enable bit.
R0 bit 3, SS, set to 1 shifts all sprites 8 pixels to the left; 0 gives normal sprite position.
R0 bits 2 and 1 are always set to 1, and bit 0, external sync, is always set to 0.
The Appendix A diagram labels R0 bit 1 as M3 and shows bits 2 and 1 as 1 and bit 0 as 0.
R0 is $36 at power on.
MAME decodes R0 bit 2 as M4, which selects mode 4, and bit 1 as M2, which selects mode 2 when M4, M1 and M3 are clear.
MAME also stops sprite collisions from being flagged in the left 8 pixels while R0 bit 5 is set.
MAME's reset fills every register, R0 included, with 0x00.
R1 bit 7 is always set to 1.
R1 bit 6, DIS, set to 0 blanks the whole screen; set to 1 gives normal video.
R1 bit 5, IE, is the interrupt enable bit.
R1 bits 4, 3 and 2 are always set to 0.
R1 bit 1, SZ, set to 0 makes all sprites 8 by 8; set to 1 makes all sprites 8 by 16.
R1 bit 0 is always set to 0.
IE 0 with IE1 1 enables the raster line interrupt; IE 1 with IE1 1 enables VBLANK and the raster line interrupt.
The Appendix A diagram marks R1 bits 4 and 3 as M1 and M2 and names bit 0 the sprite magnification bit.
R1 is $A0 at power on.
MAME decodes R1 bit 4 as M1 and bit 3 as M3; when M4 is clear, M1 alone selects mode 1 and M3 alone selects mode 3.
MAME stores a sprite zoom scale of 2 when R1 bit 0 is set and 1 otherwise.
MAME's reset fills every register, R1 included, with 0x00.
R2 sets the base address for the screen map, positioning the 2048 byte screen map at one of eight starting addresses on 2048 byte boundaries.
An R2 value of $FF puts the screen map base address at $3800.
An R2 value of $FD puts the screen map base address at $3000.
An R2 value of $FB puts the screen map base address at $2800.
An R2 value of $F9 puts the screen map base address at $2000.
An R2 value of $F7 puts the screen map base address at $1800.
An R2 value of $F5 puts the screen map base address at $1000.
An R2 value of $F3 puts the screen map base address at $0800.
An R2 value of $F1 puts the screen map base address at $0000.
The normal setting for R2 is $FF, which positions the base address at $3800, the highest-addressed 2 KByte section of the 16 KByte Video RAM.
R2 is $FF at power on.
The Appendix A diagram shows R2 as four 1 bits, three screen base bits and a 1, $FF with the screen base at $3800.
MAME's reset fills the registers with 0x00 and then sets R2 to 0x0E.
On the 315-5124 MAME ANDs the screen map row offset with a mask whose bit 10 is R2 bit 0, clearing bit 10 when R2 bit 0 is 0.
MAME takes the screen map base as (R2 << 10) & 0x3800 for 192 lines, and as ((R2 & 0x0c) << 10) | 0x0700 for other heights.
R3 should always be set to $FF.
R3 is an eight bit register, shown as $FF in the Appendix A diagram.
R3 is $FF at power on.
On the 315-5124 in mode 4 MAME ANDs the tile number with R3 shifted left by one plus 1, so a 0 bit of R3 clears a tile number bit.
MAME's reset fills every register, R3 included, with 0x00.
R4 should always be set to $FF.
R4 is an eight bit register, shown as $FF in the Appendix A diagram.
R4 is $FF at power on.
On the 315-5124 in mode 4 MAME ANDs the tile number with R4 bits 0 to 2 shifted left by 6 plus 0x3F, clearing tile bits 6 to 8.
MAME's reset fills every register, R4 included, with 0x00.
R5 controls the base address for the Sprite Attribute Table, a 256 byte table that can be positioned at one of 64 starting addresses in Video RAM.
The base address is formatted in R5 as a 1, the address bits A13 to A8, and a 1.
The normal setting for R5 is $FF, which positions the Sprite Attribute Table at $3F00.
With R2 and R5 both $FF the unused top 256 bytes of screen map memory are occupied by the 256 byte Sprite Attribute Table.
R5 is $FF at power on.
The Appendix A diagram shows R5 as a 1, six SAT base bits and a 1, $FF with the table at $3F00.
On the 315-5124 MAME adds 0x80 to the sprite attribute table base for the extra sprite data when R5 bit 0 is 1, and 0 when it is 0.
MAME's reset fills every register, R5 included, with 0x00.
MAME's sprite attribute base is (R5 << 7) & 0x3f00 in mode 4, and (R5 & 0x7f) << 7 when the video mode is below 4.
R6 sets the base address for the sprite patterns.
Only two values are valid for R6.
An R6 value of $FB puts the sprite patterns in the first 8K of Video RAM, the normal value.
An R6 value of $FF puts the sprite patterns in the second 8K of Video RAM.
The first 8K is preferred: 256 sprite patterns fit there, but only 192 fit in the second 8K, which loses 2048 bytes to the screen map and Sprite Attribute Table.
R6 is $FB at power on.
The Appendix A diagram shows R6 as five 1 bits, a character generator bank bit and two 1 bits, $FB with the patterns at $0000.
On the 315-5124 in mode 4 MAME masks the sprite tile number with R6 bits 1 and 0, so clearing either clears a tile number bit.
In mode 4 MAME adds 256 to the tile number if R6 bit 2 is set; below mode 4 it stores ((R6 & 7) << 11) + sprite_line in m_sprite_pattern_line.
MAME's reset fills every register, R6 included, with 0x00.
R7 sets the border color.
The border color is taken from the second bank of colors in VDP Color RAM.
R7 holds the border color in its low four bits, C3 to C0.
R7 is $00 at power on.
The Appendix A diagram shows R7 as four 1 bits and four border color bits, the border color.
For a set pattern bit MAME takes the pen from the high four bits of R7, and for a clear one from the low four bits.
R8 sets the horizontal scroll value for the background scene, and a value of $00 produces no scrolling.
A value of $01 moves the background scene one pixel to the left and moves the leftmost column of pixels to the rightmost column.
Higher values of R8 rotate the screen horizontally to a maximum of 255 pixels for a value of $FF.
Horizontal scrolling resembles a rotating vertical cylinder, with graphic information disappearing from the left side of the screen and reappearing on the right side.
R8 is $00 at power on.
The Appendix A diagram shows R8 as eight horizontal scroll bits, $00, with an arrow pointing left.
MAME adds R8's low three bits to each tile pixel position and starts earlier by R8 divided by 8 tile columns, so larger values move the picture right.
MAME copies R8 into m_reg8copy in its process_line_timer callback, and at once when R8 is written early in the line.
R9 sets the vertical scroll value for the background scene, and a value of $00 produces no scrolling.
A value of $01 moves the background scene one pixel upward.
The vertical scrolling resembles a rotating horizontal cylinder whose wrap around point is at the 28th character row, not at the screen edge.
Register 9 is latched in vertical blanking.
R9 is $00 at power on.
The Appendix A diagram shows R9 as eight vertical scroll bits with the value $00.
MAME copies R9 into its scroll latch when the line timer reaches the first line of the active display.
R10 controls the Raster Line Interrupt.
The picture has 192 raster lines, each followed by an HBLANK of about 10 microseconds in which the beam retraces to the left.
An interrupt just after a selected raster line has been displayed lets a program change a color after the beam has swept the top half.
Loading R10 with 94 generates a Raster Line Interrupt Request every time the 95th horizontal line finishes its scan.
The value loaded into R10 should be one less than the raster line that should trigger the interrupt.
The Raster Line Interrupt continues to generate interrupt requests as the beam sweeps the screen.
R10 values $C0 to $FF give no interrupt requests at HBLANK.
R10 value $00 requests the interrupt at HBLANK of lines 1, 2, 3 and on to 191.
R10 value $01 requests it at HBLANK of lines 2, 4, 6 and on to 190.
R10 value $02 requests it at HBLANK of lines 3, 6, 9 and on to 189.
R10 value $03 requests it at HBLANK of lines 4, 8, 12 and on to 188, and so on for higher values.
R10 value $FF turns off the interrupt requests.
R10 value $00 gives a Raster Line interrupt request for every horizontal line.
There is a one interrupt delay between loading R10 and having the value take effect.
R10 is $FF at power on.
The Appendix A diagram shows R10 as eight line interrupt bits with the value $FF, where $C1 to $FF disable the interrupt.
MAME raises the line interrupt on the first bottom border line when its line counter is 0. Top border lines reload the counter from R10; active lines count it down.
The VDP is controlled by eleven internal 8-bit registers.
The register number in a register write is r3 to r0 and ranges from 0 through 10, $00 through $0A.
MAME's constructor passes 0x0F as reg_num_mask, which control_write ANDs with the second byte before storing the data for numbers up to 0x0F.
